Routes

Every route a site calls: WallFlowers' Door at https://app.wallflowers.io, through session.fetch, which signs each request, and the public page at https://arc.wallflowers.io. The ones marked no session need nothing.

How latency was measured

Each route was called many times over each link below, warm (its connection already open) and first (a new connection: TCP and TLS first). p50 is the median, p95 the time 19 calls in 20 beat.

OverWhatThe DoorWhen

venuea delay hop at the venue's measured distance: 130 ms round trip to the Door; a rehearsal Door, a VM on the harness's machine38ad452c2026-09-30 10:12 UTC
an ordinary internet connectionproduction (app.wallflowers.io)production2026-09-30 09:49 UTC

Signing in

GET/v2/signin.jsno session

WallFlowers' sign-in script. Load it once per page, pinned by its integrity hash; it defines WallFlowers.signIn, finish and current (see Sign in). Its hash changes only with a Door release.

Request

<script src="https://app.wallflowers.io/v2/signin.js"
        integrity="sha384-tlelF9i6GEcF6TboulAVcsSZoIVw6WnnBFG/cvUqcASGz3MuwBrF8jtAh5f5RfW/"
        crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

POST/v2/tokenno session

The sign-in script calls this in WallFlowers.finish: it trades the code WallFlowers' window returned for the session token, with the page's PKCE verifier and a DPoP proof. You never call it yourself.

Answers

{ "access_token": "…", "token_type": "DPoP", "expires_in": 3600, "scope": "<community id>" }   (read by the script, never by your code)

Refusals

502with WallFlowers' own sentence
400with WallFlowers' own sentence
403 "you are neither the owner nor an admin of that Site"
401 "the code's session has ended; sign in again"
401 "the sign-in's session has ended; sign in again"

Latency (how it was measured)

Overnp50p95First call
loopback102 ms2 ms2 mseach step inside a whole flow; proof of work solved before the clock; cold here: a new client per flow, its connection opened by the untimed proof-of-work fetch
venue10139 ms145 ms139 mseach step inside a whole flow; proof of work solved before the clock; cold here: a new client per flow, its connection opened by the untimed proof-of-work fetch

Reading

GET/v2/me

The signed-in member. pk identifies them and is never a name; display_name is their name if they have set one. noncompliant lists records in reach that could not be read, with the reason: show them as unavailable. card_note is present when their picture was left out of their card, and says why.

Request

const me = await (await session.fetch('/v2/me')).json();

GET/v2/members

Your community's members as people are shown them: each one's name and picture from their card (null where they have none: show "New member", never the key), their role (owner, admin or member), their own about ({bio, links}), their answers to the community's questions (by question id), and their intentions (the choice they joined with: resources, skills or financial). The owner comes first, then the admins, then everyone else by name. questions are the owner's and admins' questions, oldest first, each with its form and the tally per option. can_define says whether the signed-in member may put a question. It is read from the same graph as /v2/graph, so it shows nothing a member could not read there, and everything in it is readable by every member of the community: say so wherever you show or edit it. Write with /v2/apply on the community: base.publishAbout {bio, links} replaces the member's whole about; base.answerQuestion {target_author, target_gen, text, choices} their whole answer; base.defineQuestion and base.retireQuestion are the owner's and admins'. Read it again after a write, or when the stream says something changed.

Request

const m = await (await session.fetch('/v2/members')).json();

Answers

{ "site": "71c1…6a6c", "me": "0224…", "can_define": false,
  "members": [
    { "key": "2d63…edfa", "name": "Hana", "icon": { "mime": "image/webp", "data": "…" }, "role": "owner",
      "about": { "bio": "I grow beans", "links": ["https://…"] },
      "answers": { "2d63…:7": { "text": null, "choices": [0, 2] } },
      "intentions": ["skills"] },
    … ],
  "questions": [
    { "id": "2d63…:7", "text": "What do you offer?", "hint": null, "options": ["Tools", "Seeds", "Time"],
      "multi": true, "max": 2, "free": false, "textMax": null, "retired": false, "tally": [3, 0, 5] } ] }

GET/v2/events

A server-sent event stream: event: changed whenever something the session can read changes. It says only that, so read /v2/graph again, about 300 ms after the last one in a burst. Use session.events(onChanged, onEnded), which carries the session (EventSource cannot); it opens the stream again by itself after a gap (2 s, doubling to a minute) and then says changed once with the version '', meaning "caught up after a gap". A 401 ends it and calls onEnded. Several streams on one session all hear the changes; one per page is plenty.

Request

const stop = session.events(onChanged, onEnded);   // stop() closes it

Answers

event: changed
data: 1790791234567

Refusals

502with WallFlowers' own sentence
401with WallFlowers' own sentence
401 "no such session"
401 "not signed in"

Writing

POST/v2/join

A claim from your community's kiosk or QR code (v1.…) joins the signed-in member to the community and to its rooms: those marked for the claim's choice or, if no room is marked for it, every unmarked room. WallFlowers sends a scanned claim to your registered home with the claim in the address's fragment, #join=…, which no request carries: read it there, sign in if the person is not signed in yet (one WallFlowers page, in your community's look: a new member names themselves and makes a passkey there, and comes straight back), then send it here. The claim is a single-use way in, so: take it off the address in your page's first script, an inline script in <head> before any other (history.replaceState(history.state, '', location.pathname + location.search), keeping history.state, which frameworks use); keep it in sessionStorage while the person signs in, never in a URL of yours and never in a log; send it only in this request's body. With a strict Content-Security-Policy, allow that inline script by its sha256. Only a claim for your own community is accepted (403 "a claim for another Site"). unjoined lists rooms not added yet: send the same claim once more a few seconds later; nothing is spent twice. A refusal is WallFlowers' sentence: show it.

Request

await session.fetch('/v2/join', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ claim }) });

Answers

{ "admitted": true, "site": "<community id>", "c": "resources", "a": null, "fallback": null,
  "rooms": [ … ], "unjoined": [], "home": "https://your.site/…" }

Refusals

404 "no join is waiting, or it has expired"

POST/v2/batch

Between 1 and 16 steps, applied in order. A later step names an object an earlier step created as {"$step": i}. If a step is refused the batch stops there, and what was made stands: retry only the steps that were not made.

Request

{ "steps": [
  { "do": "mint",  "kind": "forum", "draft": { "name": "Issue 73" } },
  { "do": "apply", "object": "<community>", "op": "base.setPart",
    "args": { "part": { "$step": 0 }, "role": "room", "at": 1790000000000 } },
  { "do": "apply", "object": { "$step": 0 }, "op": "base.setParent",
    "args": { "parent": "<community>", "role": "room", "at": 1790000000000 } } ] }

POST/v2/mint

Creates an object of a kind from its draft fields (GET /v2/draft/:kind lists them; an unknown field is refused). The session owns what it creates and reaches it until the session ends; to make it part of the community, link it in the same batch.

Creating many objects: each mint costs more as the account holds more objects: about 20 ms for a new account, about 250 ms by its tenth, 500 ms and more by its fiftieth. Make many objects in one POST /v2/batch, or send the mints together without awaiting each; never one awaited mint after another. Posting a message (POST /v2/apply) stays fast.

Request

{ "kind": "forum", "draft": { "name": "Issue 73" } }

GETarc.wallflowers.io/v1/face/:slug/itemsno session

What the public page draws, as data, readable from any origin: the community's published items by key, event:<id> (title, startMs, endMs, venue, descriptor) and post:<id>, each with its op's arguments by the model's names and at. This is how a site shows events and resources, which a member's session does not reach. Cached briefly: read it on your server and keep it a minute. Read it when the page loads, and again when something changes (session.events, on a signed-in page); never poll it faster than once every 30 s, and never in a loop. A community made at signup is published as it is made; one made before 1 October, 14:00 KST, may not be yet, and answers 404 (ask the organisers).

Request

const { items } = await (await fetch('https://arc.wallflowers.io/v1/face/mill-road/items')).json();

Routes that are not for sites

The routers serve these too. They belong to WallFlowers' own sign-in window, app and services; a site does not call them, and many refuse a site's session. This list is the routers', so it is complete.

window

WallFlowers' sign-in window: the passkey ceremony, run on app.wallflowers.io. Your page sends people there with WallFlowers.signIn.

GET /join · GET /signin/site · POST /signin/site · GET /signin · POST /v2/signin/finish · POST /v2/signin · POST /v2/signup/continue · POST /v2/signup/finish · POST /v2/signup · GET /v2/work

webapp

WallFlowers' own app. A site's session is refused on these (adding people, a person's account).

GET / · GET /index.html · POST /v2/add · POST /v2/bundle · POST /v2/history · GET /v2/site/:site/items

internal

The Door's own processes. Not reachable as an API.

POST /i/bundle · POST /i/code · POST /i/end · POST /i/forget · GET /i/key · POST /i/open · POST /i/prove · POST /i/sign · POST /i/signup/finish · POST /i/signup · GET /i/site/:site

asset

The sign-in window's own files.

GET /door/face-mark · GET /door/face.css · GET /door/perf.js · GET /door/pow-worker.js · GET /door/return-path.js · GET /door/seal.js · GET /door/signin.css · GET /door/signin.js · GET /door/wallflowers.png · GET /door/wordmark.svg

arc

The Arc's services behind WallFlowers' apps (relay, membership, console). Not an API for sites.

GET /bundle · ANY /console/*rest · POST /tether · POST /v1/admit · GET /v1/arc · GET /v1/arcs · ANY /v1/box/*rest · GET /v1/bundle · ANY /v1/console/*rest · GET /v1/health · ANY /v1/land/*rest · GET /v1/relay · POST /v1/signup · ANY /v1/systems/*rest · GET /v1/version · ANY /v1/wake/*rest
